newsitem.title: USA: U.S. green group faults USDA on CRP selections.
newsitem.headline: U.S. green group faults USDA on CRP selections.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Department made some poor selections in deciding to enroll 16.1 million acres in the Conservation Reserve Program, Environmental Defense Fund said Monday.
EDF said USDA accepted land "that scored low on environmental criteria."

EDF senior attorney Tim Searchinger said in a statement, "Particularly of concern is the department's decision to enroll 700,000 acres of land already in intensive plantation forestry operations, primarily in the Southeast, because nearly all of these lands would remain in forestry regardless."
He added, "The types of land that need environmental protection include land that can be restored in rare native habitat and very highly erodible lands."
The New York-based environmental group said it was disappointed that USDA accepted 70 percent of the land that was offered.
But, it noted, some farm-state lawmakers wanted more.
Most environmental groups last week said they were pleased that CRP would have a greated environmental focus than in the past.
USDA said it accepted 13.5 million acres of highly erodible land, including 6.56 million acres with an erodibility index of 15 or more. It also accepted 1.06 million acres for trees.
